cues.text: DNA, the instruction book for life, is made of repeating building blocks called nucleotides.
Each nucleotide has three main parts: a phosphate group, a sugar molecule, and a nitrogenous base.
These nucleotides link together, with phosphates and sugars forming a strong backbone, creating a single strand.
Two of these strands then pair up, with their bases connecting in the middle,
and twist into the famous Double Helix — a twisted ladder shape.
The secret to DNA's information storage lies in how its bases pair: Adenine (A) always pairs with Thymine (T),
and Cytosine (C) always pairs with Guanine (G).
This specific pairing creates a unique sequence along the ladder, forming the genetic code that carries all the instructions for life.
